2.modern-en: Introduced pining for Rosaline, wandering the streets melancholy. Confides in Benvolio about his unrequited love.

3.modern-en: Reads the Capulet guest list by chance and discovers Rosaline will be at the feast. Agrees to attend in disguise.

5.modern-en: Expresses foreboding about the night ahead. Mercutio tries to cheer him with the Queen Mab speech.

6.modern-en: At the Capulet ball, sees Juliet and instantly forgets Rosaline. They share their first words and a kiss before learning each is from the enemy family.

7.modern-en: Climbs the wall into the Capulet orchard, unable to leave Juliet behind.

8.modern-en: The balcony scene. Declares his love to Juliet and they exchange vows. They agree to marry the next day.

9.modern-en: Asks Friar Lawrence to marry them. The Friar agrees, hoping the union will end the feud.

10.modern-en: Encounters Mercutio and Benvolio in high spirits. The Nurse arrives and Romeo gives her the message about the secret wedding.

12.modern-en: Marries Juliet in Friar Lawrence's cell.

13.modern-en: Refuses to fight Tybalt because they are now secretly related. When Tybalt kills Mercutio, Romeo kills Tybalt in a fury and flees, crying 'I am fortune's fool.'

15.modern-en: Hides at Friar Lawrence's cell, distraught at his banishment. Threatens suicide. The Friar and Nurse talk him into going to Juliet before fleeing to Mantua.

17.modern-en: Spends his wedding night with Juliet. At dawn they part, knowing he must leave for Mantua or die.

23.modern-en: In Mantua, hears from Balthasar that Juliet is dead. Buys poison from an apothecary, determined to die beside her.

25.modern-en: Arrives at the Capulet tomb. Kills Paris who tries to stop him. Drinks poison beside Juliet's body and dies just before she wakes.

4.modern-en: Introduced as nearly fourteen. Her mother raises the subject of marriage to Paris; Juliet agrees to consider him.

6.modern-en: Meets Romeo at the ball and falls in love. Discovers he is a Montague after the dance.

8.modern-en: The balcony scene. Confesses her love for Romeo, unaware he is listening. They exchange vows and plan their secret marriage.

11.modern-en: Waits impatiently for the Nurse to return with Romeo's message. Learns the wedding is arranged for that afternoon.

12.modern-en: Arrives at Friar Lawrence's cell and marries Romeo.

14.modern-en: Learns from the Nurse that Tybalt is dead and Romeo is banished. Torn between grief for her cousin and love for her husband, ultimately sides with Romeo.

17.modern-en: After the wedding night, parts from Romeo at dawn. Refuses her father's order to marry Paris. Is threatened with disownment. The Nurse advises her to marry Paris; Juliet resolves to seek the Friar's help.

18.modern-en: Goes to Friar Lawrence. He gives her a potion that will make her appear dead for forty-two hours, during which Romeo will be sent for.

19.modern-en: Returns home and pretends to agree to the marriage with Paris.

20.modern-en: Alone, overcomes her fears and drinks the potion.

22.modern-en: Found apparently dead by the Nurse and her family. The wedding turns to a funeral.

25.modern-en: Wakes in the tomb to find Romeo dead beside her. Kisses his poisoned lips, then stabs herself with his dagger.

epithet.en: Romeo's friend, kinsman of the Prince

5.modern-en: Delivers the famous Queen Mab speech, a dazzling, increasingly dark fantasy about the fairy queen who brings dreams. Tries to shake Romeo out of his melancholy.

7.modern-en: Calls for Romeo in the dark after the feast, mocking his lovesickness for Rosaline.

10.modern-en: Teases Romeo about his overnight disappearance. Engages in witty wordplay with the Nurse.

13.modern-en: Provokes Tybalt when Romeo refuses to fight. Is fatally stabbed under Romeo's arm when Romeo tries to intervene. Dies cursing both houses: 'A plague on both your houses!'

2.modern-en: Draws his sword eagerly in the opening street brawl, ready to fight any Montague.

6.modern-en: Recognizes Romeo at the Capulet ball by his voice. Capulet forbids him from causing a scene, but Tybalt vows future revenge.

13.modern-en: Challenges Romeo to a duel. When Romeo refuses, fights Mercutio instead and kills him. Returns and is killed by Romeo.

9.modern-en: Introduced gathering herbs at dawn. Agrees to marry Romeo and Juliet, hoping it will reconcile the feuding families.

12.modern-en: Performs the secret wedding ceremony for Romeo and Juliet.

15.modern-en: Tells Romeo his banishment is mercy, not punishment. Devises a plan: Romeo will go to Juliet, then flee to Mantua until the marriage can be revealed.

18.modern-en: Gives Juliet the sleeping potion and promises to send a message to Romeo in Mantua explaining the plan.

22.modern-en: Arrives at the Capulet house to find the family mourning Juliet's apparent death.

24.modern-en: Learns that his letter to Romeo never reached Mantua because Friar John was quarantined. Rushes to the tomb.

25.modern-en: Arrives at the tomb too late. Finds Romeo dead and tries to convince the waking Juliet to leave. Flees when the watch approaches. Later confesses everything to the Prince.

4.modern-en: Rambles affectionately about Juliet's childhood. Supports Lady Capulet's suggestion that Juliet consider Paris.

6.modern-en: Identifies Romeo as a Montague for Juliet after the ball.

10.modern-en: Goes to Romeo to arrange the wedding details. Endures Mercutio's teasing. Returns with the message for Juliet.

11.modern-en: Torments Juliet by delaying the good news. Finally tells her to go to Friar Lawrence's cell to be married.

14.modern-en: Brings Juliet news of Tybalt's death and Romeo's banishment. Agrees to bring Romeo to Juliet's chamber.

15.modern-en: Comes to Friar Lawrence's cell to fetch Romeo for Juliet.

17.modern-en: Warns the lovers that Lady Capulet is coming. Later advises Juliet to forget Romeo and marry Paris, losing Juliet's trust.

19.modern-en: Helps Juliet prepare for the supposed wedding to Paris.

20.modern-en: Present when Juliet asks to be left alone for the night.

21.modern-en: Helps with wedding preparations through the night.

22.modern-en: Discovers Juliet apparently dead in her bed and raises the alarm.

epithet.en: Head of the Capulet family, Juliet's father

2.modern-en: Enters the street brawl calling for his sword. Restrained by his wife.

3.modern-en: Tells Paris that Juliet is young but invites him to the feast to begin his courtship.

6.modern-en: Hosts the ball. Stops Tybalt from attacking Romeo, insisting on civil behavior under his roof.

16.modern-en: Arranges Juliet's marriage to Paris for Thursday, hoping it will lift her spirits after Tybalt's death.

17.modern-en: Furiously threatens to disown Juliet when she refuses to marry Paris.

19.modern-en: Overjoyed when Juliet appears to consent. Moves the wedding up to Wednesday.

21.modern-en: Stays up all night overseeing wedding preparations.

22.modern-en: Devastated to find Juliet dead on her wedding morning.

25.modern-en: At the tomb, learns the full truth. Offers his hand to Montague, ending the feud.

2.modern-en: Tries to hold Capulet back from joining the street brawl.

4.modern-en: Broaches the subject of marriage to Paris with Juliet, praising his qualities.

16.modern-en: Tells Juliet about the planned marriage to Paris.

17.modern-en: Refuses to intercede with Capulet on Juliet's behalf when she protests the marriage.

20.modern-en: Bids Juliet goodnight before the supposed wedding day.

25.modern-en: Present at the tomb for the final revelations.

epithet.en: Head of the Montague family, Romeo's father

2.modern-en: Enters the street brawl. Afterwards, worries about Romeo's melancholy and asks Benvolio to find out what troubles him.

13.modern-en: Present at the Prince's judgment after the deaths of Mercutio and Tybalt.

25.modern-en: Arrives at the tomb. Reveals his wife has died of grief over Romeo's banishment. Offers to raise a golden statue of Juliet, making peace with Capulet.

2.modern-en: Tries to stop the opening street brawl. Afterwards, promises Montague he will find out what troubles Romeo.

3.modern-en: Encourages Romeo to attend the Capulet feast to see other beauties and forget Rosaline.

5.modern-en: Accompanies Romeo and Mercutio to the Capulet ball.

7.modern-en: Calls for Romeo after the feast, then gives up and leaves.

10.modern-en: Banters with Mercutio while waiting for Romeo.

13.modern-en: Witnesses Mercutio's death and Romeo's killing of Tybalt. Gives the Prince an account of what happened.

3.modern-en: Asks Capulet for Juliet's hand. Capulet says she is too young but invites him to the feast.

16.modern-en: Meets Capulet to discuss the marriage, which is now arranged for Thursday.

18.modern-en: Encounters Juliet at Friar Lawrence's cell. She avoids his advances.

22.modern-en: Arrives for the wedding to find Juliet apparently dead. Mourns her alongside the family.

25.modern-en: Stands watch at Juliet's tomb to mourn. Confronts Romeo when he arrives and is killed in the fight.

2.modern-en: Arrives to stop the street brawl. Declares that the next outbreak of violence between the families will be punished by death.

13.modern-en: Pronounces judgment after Tybalt's death: Romeo is banished from Verona rather than executed, because Tybalt killed first.

25.modern-en: Arrives at the tomb, hears Friar Lawrence's confession, and declares that all are punished by the tragedy. Brokers the peace between the families.

epithet.en: Romeo's first love, never seen on stage

2.modern-en: The unseen object of Romeo's lovesickness. She has sworn to live chaste, which leaves Romeo despairing.

24.modern-en: Returns to tell Friar Lawrence that he was quarantined due to plague fears and could not deliver the crucial letter to Romeo in Mantua.

epithet.en: A poor seller of drugs in Mantua

23.modern-en: Reluctantly sells Romeo a deadly poison for forty ducats, despite it being illegal, because he is desperately poor.
